feedback: If you leave 2 + 3 × 4 as 14 or add brackets that don't change anything, place them side by side: (2 + 3) × 4 = 20 forces the addition first; 2 + (3 × 4) = 14 does not.
Check your target: (2 + 3) × 4 computes 2 + 3 = 5 first, then 5 × 4 = 20.
Say which operation the brackets made happen first and why that reorders the calculation.
activities.intendedInsight: Brackets are a genuine structural operation that overrides the default order — WHERE they go determines which operation happens first, so they change the result rather than being optional punctuation.
learnerActions: Start with 2 + 3 × 4 and position bracket handles around different parts of the expression.
Compare (2 + 3) × 4 = 20 against 2 + (3 × 4) = 14, reading the result each time.
Given the numbers 2, 3, 4 with + and ×, slide the brackets until the expression equals a target of 20.
State in your own words why where the brackets sit changes the answer.
activities.title: Bracket playground: move the brackets, watch the value change

feedback: If you get 17 for 3 × (4 + 5), you multiplied before the bracket — the grouped part must become a single number (9) before anything outside it.

If you multiplied 2 × 3 first in the nested one (getting 6 + 6 = 12), you worked outside-in; always cross out the innermost pair first and rewrite with its value. (Combining 3 + 7 first happens to give the same 18 here, because adding and subtracting can be regrouped, but follow the innermost-first routine.)
A right sequence with a wrong sum inside a bracket is just an arithmetic slip — recompute that one bracket, don't restart the whole routine.
activities.intendedInsight: Nested grouping is resolved from the innermost pair outward; replacing each completed group with its value keeps the calculation tidy and prevents dropping or mismatching a level.
learnerActions: Evaluate 3 × (4 + 5) by computing inside the parentheses first: 4 + 5 = 9, then 3 × 9 = 27.
Evaluate the nested expression 2 × [3 + (7 − 1)] by resolving the innermost pair first: (7 − 1) = 6, then [3 + 6] = 9, then 2 × 9 = 18.
After each step, rewrite the whole expression with the collapsed group replaced by its single value before continuing.
Colour-code or circle matching bracket pairs so you never mismatch or skip a level.
activities.title: Collapse the innermost group: evaluating nested expressions inside-out

feedback: If you can't reach the target, ask which operation needs to happen first and wrap that part: for 20, the 2 + 3 must be grouped so it becomes 5 before multiplying by 4.
Compare your result against the no-bracket value (14) to confirm the brackets actually changed the order.
State the reorder explicitly: '(2 + 3) × 4 does the addition first, giving 5 × 4 = 20.'
activities.intendedInsight: Inserting brackets to reach a required value shows that grouping genuinely reorders a calculation: under the convention that multiplication comes before addition, 2 + 3 × 4 is 14, and only grouping (2 + 3) makes it 20. Note that working strictly left to right also gives 20 here, so the learner must write the brackets and explain them; reaching 20 alone does not show the brackets were understood.
learnerActions: Take 2 + 3 × 4 (which without brackets equals 14, using the convention that multiplication is done before addition) and insert parentheses to make it equal 20.
Write out the bracketed version, then evaluate it step by step to confirm it reaches the target.
Explain which operation your brackets forced to happen first, and why that changes the answer from 14 to 20.
Try a second target on a fresh set of numbers and justify your placement.
activities.title: Insert brackets to hit a target and explain why

feedback: For the fill-in, check that (7 − 1) = 6 was done before [3 + 6] = 9, then 2 × 9 = 18.
When correcting an error, point to exactly which step used the wrong (outer-first) order.

Choosing a correct option can confirm you recognise the right placement but does not by itself show you can construct bracket placements independently — also do an insertion task where you place the brackets yourself.
activities.intendedInsight: Grouped and nested evaluations, and bracket-placement choices, can be checked precisely, including incorrect options that reflect outside-in evaluation and ignored brackets.
learnerActions: Fill in the value of {2 × [3 + (7 − 1)]} and show each inside-out step.
Choose which bracket placement makes 2 + 3 × 4 equal 20 from a set of options.
Spot and correct an expression that was evaluated outside-in instead of innermost-first.
activities.title: Checkable practice and spot-the-error
